title: Competition BBQ Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: Competition BBQ Chicken Thighs | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Comp-turn thighs that hold warm and still look pro on the tray
subtitle: Skinned thighs, sweet rub, and glaze finish for ten judges—or ten firefighters
description: Adapted from classic competition chicken thigh tradition (Traeger, Meat Church): bone-in thighs get trimmed and squared, rubbed, smoked at 275°F, glazed, and finished until skin bites and meat hits 175°F.

steps.title: Trim competition-style
steps.instruction: Skin thighs and trim excess fat and flap meat for uniform pieces about 4 oz each. Square edges so they cook evenly. Pat dry.

steps.title: Apply sweet rub
steps.instruction: Mix salt, brown sugar, paprika, garlic, onion, and cayenne. Coat thighs evenly. Rest 15 minutes while smoker heats to 275°F.

steps.title: Smoke to 150°F
steps.instruction: Smoke thighs at 275°F until internal temp reaches 150°F and color looks even, about 45–55 minutes.

steps.title: Build competition glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer honey, BBQ sauce, vinegar, and butter until glossy. Keep warm for basting.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Brush thighs with glaze. Finish at 375°F on smoker or grill 8–10 minutes until glaze sets and internal temp hits 175°F.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest thighs 5 minutes. Hold covered at 170°F with foil vented slightly until service.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Arrange thighs on a tray, glaze side up. Extra glaze on the side for dipping.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Pull meat for wraps. Reheat covered at 325°F until 165°F internal.

proTips: 175°F for dark meat thighs—165°F can read chewy on competition-style trims.
Square pieces cook and glaze evenly; ragged thighs burn at the tips.
Keep glaze warm but not boiling or honey will taste bitter.
tonightSpread: Glazed thighs on a sheet pan.
Extra glaze in a ramekin for dipping.
leftovers: Chop into chicken salad with celery and grapes.
Slice onto Caesar salad for a smoky lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thighs are competition forgiving and hall practical. They hold covered at 170°F and still eat tender after a long hold.
mealPrepNotes: Trim thighs early. Smoke in two batches if needed. Hold finished thighs covered at 170°F up to 45 minutes; glaze right before service.
